mismatches.expected: A plain string, or an object keyed `sectorName`.
mismatches.actual: An object keyed `name` (plus `compId`, `id`, `description`) - e.g. {"compId":82,"id":211,"name":"Aerospace & Defence","description":"Aerospace & Defence"}. Confirmed identical on 574 and 9453.
mismatches.impact: buildIndustry() maps `s?.sectorName` over every element, gets null for all of them, and returns null. The Industry row on the company sidebar is therefore EMPTY for every company that has no curated entry - i.e. all but the 2 in src/data/company-profiles.ts. The API data is present and correct; the read is looking at the wrong key.
mismatches.where: src/services/company-profile.ts - buildIndustry(), and the ApiCompany.sectors declaration

mismatches.expected: Socials come only from /details, which is why a second request is made per company render.
mismatches.actual: /api/Companies/{id} ALREADY returns blog, facebook, twitter, youTube, linkedIn, telegram - the same six fields, with the same values as /details on company 82.
mismatches.impact: The /details request is redundant for socials. Its only other contribution is `otc` and the established/listed/employees trio, all of which came back empty on every company sampled. Dropping it would remove one HTTP request per company page.
mismatches.where: src/services/company-profile.ts - buildSocials(), and the getJsonOrNull call for /details

mismatches.expected: Declared and read as an alternative to companyName, described as "the bug behind every company page rendering Company {id}".
mismatches.actual: Never returned by the live endpoint. `companyName` is always populated (verified on 82, 574, 14, 9453).
mismatches.impact: None - the pick() fallback is harmless. The named bug is not reproducible today; company names resolve correctly.

mismatches.actual: VERIFIED: { compId, id, bloombergCode, name } - e.g. {"bloombergCode":"CST","name":"Construction & Engineering"}. The defensive `bloombergCode` branch is correct.
mismatches.impact: Works, but `name` (the human-readable label) is discarded, so seven codes render as seven rows all labelled "Bloomberg": ASIA, COS, CST, NRG, JAPAN, JPS, MAC. Using `name` as the label would make the card readable.

mismatches.actual: Also returns pos1Name, pos1Desc, pos2Name, pos2Desc (officer name/title slots). On company 82: pos1Desc "CEO", pos2Desc "CEO", both names empty.
The object also carries page: 1, size: 20, sort1: "", ord1: "ASC" - list-endpoint parameters leaking into a single-entity response.

mismatches.expected: Not part of the public contract.
mismatches.actual: Returned in plaintext on the UNAUTHENTICATED endpoint. Company 82 returns a real username and password pair.
mismatches.impact: Credential disclosure to anyone who can reach the API. Already logged in PROJECT-CONTEXT.toon security.findings; re-confirmed live on 2026-09-10 and still present. Values are redacted in this export.
mismatches.fix: Backend must strip these from the Companies DTO. Nothing the frontend can do.

mismatches.expected: Code comment: "by-company does not return a language field, so this is only populated on paths that have one - today that means search results."
mismatches.actual: It DOES return `language` ("EN" on both rows sampled). mapArticle() never reads it, so CompanyArticle.language stays undefined.
mismatches.impact: Language tags are suppressed on every row of every company feed even though the data is available. One line in mapArticle() would restore them.

mismatches.actual: Returns the FULL article: body, bodyText, bodyHtml, subHeadLine, sourceId, sectors, topicName, sourceName as well. Two rows cost 20.5 KB.
mismatches.impact: A 15-row company page transfers roughly 150 KB where ~8 KB would do. No correctness issue, but the feed could render richer rows (subheadline, sectors) for free since the bytes already arrive.

mismatches.expected: NewApiArticle declares companyId/logoFilename for list endpoints and companyID/logoFileName for the detail endpoint, both optional as a defence.
mismatches.actual: by-company uses the DETAIL spelling: companyID / logoFileName.
mismatches.impact: None here - mapArticle() reads neither. Confirms the defensive both-spellings declaration is warranted.
